issue.title: fix: allow trailing tabs on setext underlines (CommonMark §4.3)
issue.body:
## Summary
CommonMark §4.3 allows a setext underline to end with spaces or tabs. Marked only accepted trailing spaces, so `Foo` + `===\t` stayed a paragraph and `Foo` + `---\t` became a paragraph plus a thematic break instead of `<h1>` / `<h2>`. The same miss affected block quotes (`> Bar` / `> ===\t`).

## Fix
`lheadingCore` and the lazy-underline mask now accept trailing tabs the same way they accept spaces. Spec example 86 only uses spaces, so the suite never caught this; a dedicated fixture covers the tab case.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` (1913 spec + 199 unit)
- [x] `npm run lint`

issue.title: fix(core): invalidate cached hashes when a symlink target changes
issue.body:
## Current Behavior

Editing the file a symlinked input points to does not change the symlink's own mtime. The file-hash archive keys entries on that mtime, so Nx restores the output built from the old content until `.nx/workspace-data` is cleared.

## Expected Behavior

A stored hash is reused only while the symlink target is unchanged. The walker stamps a symlink with the later of the link's mtime and the target's mtime, so editing the target or retargeting the link misses the archive and the file is hashed again.

## Related Issue(s)

Fixes #37460

comment.body: Compare symlink and target mtimes independently so staged link replacement is still detected. Ready for another look.

issue.title: fix(core): hash package.json script bodies when targets set their own inputs
issue.body:
## Current Behavior

An `nx:run-script` target inferred from a `package.json` script stores only the script name in `options` (`{ script: "build" }`). The command itself lives in `metadata.scriptContent`. The project-configuration hash covers the executor, outputs, options, configurations, and parallelism, but not that body.

If the target sets its own inputs and those inputs do not include `package.json`, editing the script body does not change the task hash. `nx run-many -t build` restores the previous output from the local cache and the new command never runs.

## Expected Behavior

The script body is part of the task. Changing it changes the hash and the task runs again, including when the target defines its own inputs. Targets with no script body keep their existing hash.

## Related Issue(s)

Fixes #37457

issue.title: fix(core): close pseudo-terminal fds when commands exit
issue.body:
## Current Behavior

Every command Nx runs through its native pseudo terminal opens a pty, and the pty's master and slave fds stay open until `RustPseudoTerminal` is garbage-collected. A long-lived process that keeps finished task objects (for example `nx run:dev` through `nx:run-commands`) leaks `/dev/ptmx` descriptors. On macOS that exhausts `kern.tty.ptmx_max` and other programs fail with `fork failed: Device not configured`.

## Expected Behavior

When a pseudo terminal's last child exits, its pty fds are closed immediately, even if the terminal and child-process objects are still referenced. A later command on the same terminal opens a new pty. The `/dev/ptmx` count returns to baseline without waiting for GC.

## Related Issue(s)

Fixes #37786

issue.title: fix: keep command tuple rest elements last
issue.body:
This pull request fixes https://github.com/redis/ioredis/issues/1570.

TypeScript 4.1 reports `TS1256: A rest element must be last in a tuple type` while checking `RedisCommander`. Command overloads were tuples of the form `[fixed arguments, ...rest, later options, callback]`. TypeScript 4.2 and newer accept a rest element in the middle. TypeScript 4.1 does not, so a project on 4.1.3 fails to compile any file that imports ioredis.

Trailing option and callback types are now part of the rest element, which makes that rest element last. Calls that pass variadic arguments, then options, then an optional callback still typecheck. Overloads that take those keys or fields as a real array still require the original positions. The client still reads a callback only when it is the last argument.

Spread overloads accept those option tokens anywhere in the variadic list. Array overloads continue to require them in order.

Fixes #1570

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> **Medium Risk**
> Rewrites generated interface signatures via a large string parser, so any parsing edge case could break typings; limited to build-time output but affects all consumers of `RedisCommander.ts`.

> **Generator updates:** `bin/index.js` pipes every freshly generated `RedisCommander.ts` through a new `ensureRestElementsLast` transform so the emitted overload tuples always end with their rest spreads. **`bin/restElement.js`** implements that rewrite by folding trailing option/callback members into `[...Rest, …]` spreads, synthesizing `Rest extends …` type parameters when needed, rebinding placeholders, and reordering clustered overloads so precise signatures stay ahead of looser callback variants.

issue.title: fix(virtual-core): stop scroll corrections from ping-ponging on a stale layout box
issue.body:
Fixes the scroll-correction loop in #1252.

When a virtualized row is taller or shorter than `estimateSize` (wrapping cells, sticky group headers), the virtualizer compensates by writing `scrollTop` from the resize observer. That write is flushed in the same turn, so the next measurement reads the layout box the correction just invalidated and reports the size the row just left. The opposite delta is applied, the new size comes back, and the corrections alternate (`correction 3` / `correction -3` in the issue recording) until the main thread is stuck. Pausing script execution for a frame lets layout settle, which matches a stale box rather than a real size change. The pinned header jumps by that delta on every turn.

Keep the size that was just committed when a re-entrant notify, or a later observation in the same ResizeObserver broadcast, reports exactly the size the item just left. After that broadcast, read the settled border box on the next frame and apply it once. A direct `resizeItem` back to an earlier size, outside that echo, still applies immediately.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run` in `packages/virtual-core` (478 passed, 1 skipped)
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run` in `packages/react-virtual` (11 passed)
- [x] `eslint` and `tsc --noEmit` for `packages/virtual-core`
- Re-entrant notify that flips the measured size does not loop
- The next ResizeObserver delivery of the previous size does not reverse the correction
- The following frame adopts a settled size exactly once
- A later direct resize back to a previous size still applies

Fixes #1252

issue.title: [expo-modules-autolinking][expo-modules-core][expo-dev-launcher] Compile Gradle plugins with Kotlin 2.4.20

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: PR author is not a member of the expo GitHub org

issue.body:
# Why

Android configuration fails on Gradle 9.7 and later. `compileKotlin` for Expo's included Gradle plugins stops with a Kotlin metadata error.

Those plugins compile with Kotlin 2.2. Gradle 9.7 embeds Kotlin 2.4.0, and Gradle 9.8 embeds Kotlin 2.4.10. A Kotlin 2.2 compiler can read metadata up to 2.3.0, so it cannot read that standard library.

# How

The issue names Kotlin 2.4.20, and the reporter's patch uses that version. Kotlin 2.4.20 can read Kotlin 2.4 metadata. A newer compiler can also read the older standard library in Gradle 9.4.1, which the current template uses.

The diff sets `kotlin("jvm")` to 2.4.20 for each included plugin build:

- `expo-modules-autolinking` (`expo-gradle-plugin`)
- `expo-modules-core`
- `expo-dev-launcher`
- `expo-updates` (this pin was 2.2.0)
- `expo-network-addons`
- `expo-brownfield`

It sets `kotlin("plugin.serialization")` in `expo-autolinking-plugin-shared` to 2.4.20. The `kotlinx-serialization-json` runtime stays at 1.6.3.

`expo-ktlint-rules` stays on Kotlin 2.2.21. It is the ktlint rule set included by Expo Go and bare-expo, those apps use Gradle 9.4.1, and the rules target the Kotlin 1.9 language level because they run on ktlint 1.0.1.

The pins move together. After one included plugin compiles, the next one fails the same way. This only changes the compiler used to build the plugins. It does not change app bytecode.

# Test Plan

Linux, OpenJDK 21. No Android SDK, no emulator, and no device. `npx expo prebuild` was not run.

Gradle 9.8.1 embeds Kotlin 2.4.10. With Kotlin 2.2.21, `:expo-autolinking-settings-plugin:compileKotlin` failed. The compiler reported metadata 2.4.0 on `kotlin.Pair` and on `kotlin-stdlib-2.4.10.jar`.

With Kotlin 2.4.20, on Gradle 9.8.1, these tasks succeeded:

- `:expo-autolinking-settings-plugin:compileKotlin`
- `:expo-autolinking-plugin-shared:compileKotlin`
- `:expo-autolinking-plugin:compileKotlin`
- `:expo-max-sdk-override-plugin:compileKotlin`
- `:brownfield:compileKotlin` and `:brownfield:test` (3 tests passed)
- `:publish:compileKotlin` for the brownfield publish plugin

Autolinking plugin unit tests that do not need the package JavaScript build passed (27 tests). `ExpoAutolinkingSettingsPluginTest` (4 tests) failed in setup because `packages/expo-modules-autolinking/build` is absent. The monorepo was not installed, and that package was not built with `pnpm`.

`expo-module-gradle-plugin`, `expo-dev-launcher-gradle-plugin`, `expo-updates-gradle-plugin`, and `expo-network-addons-gradle-plugin` compiled with Kotlin 2.4.20 on Gradle 9.4.1. They depend on `@react-native/gradle-plugin` 0.88.1, which still applies Kotlin 2.2.0, so that included build cannot compile on Gradle 9.8.1.

# Screenshots

No UI change.

- [x] I added a changeset and followed [this short guide](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-before-submitting)
- [ ] This diff will work correctly for `npx expo prebuild` & EAS Build (eg: updated a module plugin).
- [ ] Conforms with the [Documentation Writing Style Guide](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/main/guides/Expo%20Documentation%20Writing%20Style%20Guide.md)

Fixes #52590

issue.title: fix(core): include a file's executable bit in its hash
issue.body:
## Current Behavior

A task hash ignores file modes. After `chmod +x` or `chmod -x` on an input, Nx hits the local cache and restores outputs built for the old mode. `chmod` changes neither the file's bytes nor its mtime, and the files archive and the ignored-file index both reuse a stored hash when the mtime (and, for the index, the size) still match. The run exits 0. The same thing happens with the change uncommitted and after it is committed. git records the mode.

## Expected Behavior

On Unix, the executable bit is part of an input's identity, as it is in git (`mode & 0o111 != 0`). Changing only that bit moves the file hash, misses both stamps, and moves the task hash. A non-executable file keeps its content-only hash. Off Unix, file hashes and stamps are unchanged.

## Related Issue(s)

Fixes #37459

issue.title: [expo-location][Android] Stop the foreground service after the OS restarts the app

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: PR author is not a member of the expo GitHub org

issue.body:
# Why

`stopLocationUpdatesAsync` leaves `LocationTaskService` and its notification running after the OS restarts the app.

`stopForegroundService()` only calls `mService.stop()`. The restarted service uses `START_REDELIVER_INTENT`. The new process does not bind, because `maybeStartForegroundService()` returns while the app is in the background. `mService` stays null, so Stop does nothing.

# How

Binding to a service that is already running would keep that service connected from the background. That path is what the background check is there to avoid. `context.stopService` matches the Stop request and does not start another foreground service.

`context.stopService(Intent(context, LocationTaskService::class.java))` runs when `mService` is null and this process has no bind in flight. `stopService` does nothing when the service is not running, so a second Stop is safe. One call to ActivityManager on Stop. No cost while tracking is running.

A bind started in this process is left alone. `onServiceConnected` stops the service after `onStartCommand` calls `startForeground`. `stopService` before that can crash the app with `ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTimeException`.

The diff changes `stopForegroundService()` only. It does not change `maybeStartForegroundService()` or `onHostResume()`. Pull request #52634 edits those for a different bug.

Every Android device that uses this foreground service needs the change. The system can kill and restart the process on any device. The code path is shared.

The changelog entry is under Unpublished, Bug fixes. The changeset is a patch for `expo-location`.

issue.title: [expo-print][Android] Fix print hanging when a garbage collection runs during the render

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: PR author is not a member of the expo GitHub org

issue.body:
# Why

`printToFileAsync` on Android sometimes never settles. The same call can reject with "An error occurred while writing the PDF data". The HTML branch of `print` uses the same render task.

`printToFile` and the HTML branch of `print` keep `PrintPDFRenderTask` as a local variable. `render` creates an off-screen `WebView` and returns. After that return, no GC root reaches the task, the `WebView`, or the write callbacks. A garbage collection before `onWriteFinished` drops the `WebView`, and the continuation never resumes. A collection during the write calls `onWriteFailed`, and the call rejects.

# How

Keep each `PrintPDFRenderTask` in a module-level set until that render settles. The set is a GC root for the life of the module, so the off-screen `WebView` stays alive until the render finishes. `ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet()` makes add and remove safe when cancellation and the `WebView` callback run on different threads. Each in-flight render adds one strong reference. The set is empty when nothing is rendering.

`printToFile` and the HTML branch of `print` add the task before `render`. Both remove it in `onRenderFinished`, `onRenderError`, and `invokeOnCancellation`. They also remove it when `render` throws. In `print`, `onRenderFinished` releases the task before `PrintManager.print` takes the adapter. The print framework then owns the document.

This matches the lifecycle in the issue. The diff changes `PrintModule.kt`, adds an Unpublished bug-fix entry to the changelog, and adds a patch changeset.

# Test Plan

Android did not run. This environment has no Android SDK and no emulator.

On Linux, `pnpm exec turbo run lint typecheck test depscheck build --filter=expo-print` finished with 54 successful tasks. `expo-print` lint reported 0 warnings and 0 errors. `pnpm exec turbo run format --filter=expo-print -- --check` reported that all matched files use the correct format. `pnpm changeset status` lists `expo-print` as a patch from `.changeset/expo-print-android-retain-render-task.md`.

issue.title: fix(core): resolve package roots when exports hide package.json
issue.body:
## Current Behavior

`TargetProjectLocator.readPackageJson` resolves `path.join(packageName, 'package.json')`. On POSIX that's a real subpath specifier, so for a package whose `exports` don't include `./package.json` (for example `@stencil/core` 4.44.2) Node throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. The fallback then walks up from the main entry and stops at the first manifest with a `name` and `version`, which can be a nested one such as `@stencil/core/internal`. The dependency is attributed to the wrong package, and `enforce-module-boundaries` with `banTransitiveDependencies` flags a package that is actually a direct dependency. On Windows `path.join` produces a backslash specifier, which happens to sidestep `exports`, so the behavior differs by OS.

## Expected Behavior

- The specifier is always built with `/`, so every OS honors `exports` the same way.
- If that lookup fails or only finds a module-format stub, the locator reads the install root (`node_modules/<name>/package.json`) derived from the resolved entry path. This also works with pnpm's store layout, and aliases keep that file's own name.
- While walking up, a manifest whose `name` is a subpath of the requested package is skipped instead of returned.
- Packages that do export `./package.json` keep using that file as before.

Added a test in `target-project-locator.spec.ts` for a package that hides `package.json` behind `exports` and ships a nested manifest; it failed before the change and the full spec (204 tests) passes after it.

Fixes #37488

issue.title: fix(core): only remove nx-owned files on nx reset
issue.body:
## Current Behavior

`nx reset` calls `rmSync(cacheDir, { recursive: true, force: true })` on the configured cache directory. Because `cacheDirectory` (or `NX_CACHE_DIRECTORY`) can point at a directory that also holds other files, reset wipes the directory and everything in it, including files Nx never wrote.

## Expected Behavior

`nx reset` removes only the entries Nx itself puts in the cache directory and leaves the directory and anything else inside it alone:

- task-hash output directories (decimal xxh3 hashes, plus older hex hashes)
- `<hash>.commit` markers and `<hash>.tar.zst` archives
- `terminalOutputs/`, `batchOutputs/`, and `run.json`
- `.nx-write-probe-*` files
- versioned database files (`{id}-v{schema}.db` and its `-wal` / `-shm` / `-journal` / `.lock` companions)

A regular file that happens to have a hash-like name is kept, since Nx stores task outputs as directories. Symlinks are unlinked rather than followed, and if the cache path itself is a symlink it is left in place. When the shared cache is active, the checkout's own `.nx/cache` gets the same treatment instead of being deleted wholesale.

Tests: added `reset-cache-entries.spec.ts` covering what is and isn't removed, and updated `reset.spec.ts`. Both pass with vitest, and the prepush checks (format, lint, commit message) pass.

Fixes #37467

issue.title: fix: don't treat an escaped ) or quote as an inline link or title closer
issue.body:
**Marked version:** master (2f90743)

**Markdown flavor:** CommonMark

## Description

No existing issue that I could find.

## Expectation

A backslash-escaped `)` or quote is literal text, so it can't end an inline link destination or a link title. Per CommonMark, `[foo](/url\)` has no closing paren and should render as plain text, and `[a](b "t\")` has an unterminated title.

## Result

marked accepts the escaped character as the closer:

- `[foo](/url\)` renders as a link to `/url%5C`
- `[a](b "t\")`, `[a](b 't\')`, and `[a](b (title\))` render as links with a title
- `[foo]: /url "t\"` is accepted as a definition with a title

## What was attempted

- The inline link tokenizer now bails out when the `)` that ends the match is preceded by an odd number of backslashes.
- The inline link and link definition title patterns now let a backslash consume the next character instead of an optional closer, so an escaped delimiter can't end the title.

Cases that should keep working still do: `[a](b (ti\)tle))`, `[link](foo\)\:)`, `[foo](/url\\)` (escaped backslash, then a real closer), and `[link](foo)\)`.

issue.title: feat(lit-virtual): add setOptions to update virtualizer options after construction
issue.body:
## 🎯 Changes

Fixes #1251.

`VirtualizerController` only took options in its constructor, so options that come from reactive Lit properties (`count`, `estimateSize`, `horizontal`, and so on) never reached the virtualizer after the first render. Calling `getVirtualizer().setOptions(...)` directly isn't a workaround, because it replaces the options wholesale and drops the controller's `onChange` wrapper that re-renders the host.

This adds `setOptions` to `VirtualizerController` and `WindowVirtualizerController`:

- It merges a partial update over the options the controller already holds (including the element/window defaults), and skips `undefined` values so a partial update can't wipe a stored option.
- It re-wraps `onChange` so the host still re-renders, pushes the merged options to the virtualizer, and calls `_willUpdate()`.
- Called from `willUpdate` it doesn't schedule an extra host update, since that render pass hasn't happened yet. Called anywhere else it requests one.

```ts
protected willUpdate(changed: PropertyValues<this>) {
  if (changed.has('count')) {
    this.virtualizerController.setOptions({ count: this.count })
  }
}
```

This picks up the feedback on #1253 (closed without merging): the test now checks the rendered total size (500 then 1000) instead of waiting for an item index the viewport can't show, the changeset is `minor` because it's new public API, and `docs/framework/lit/lit-virtual.md` plus the package README now cover `setOptions` and why to use it instead of `getVirtualizer().setOptions(...)`.

issue.title: [@mantine/core] TagsInput: Fix readOnly not preventing value changes on paste

labels.name: repo-2d2f2fa2
labels.description: Reviewed and verified PR

issue.body:
When `TagsInput` has `readOnly` set, typing and removing tags are blocked, but pasting still goes through `handlePaste`, which calls `preventDefault()` and then splits the clipboard text and adds the pieces as new tags. So a read-only TagsInput could still have its value changed (and `onChange` fired) by pasting something like `Angular,Vue`.

This returns early from `handlePaste` when `readOnly` is true, after calling the user's `onPaste` handler and before touching the value. The native paste is a no-op on a read-only input, so nothing gets inserted.

Added a test that pastes into a read-only TagsInput and checks the existing tag is unchanged, no new tags appear, and `onChange` isn't called.

issue.title: fix(linter/react): ignore impure calls in async components in react/purity
issue.body:
Fixes #27974

`react/purity` flags `Date.now()`, `new Date()`, and `Math.random()` inside async function components. An async component is a Server Component: it renders once per request and never re-renders, so those calls aren't a render-stability problem there.

The purity check now gets turned off in `compile_fn` when the function being compiled is an async component (`hir.is_async` and `ReactFunctionType::Component`). Nested functions are analysed with the same config, so callbacks such as a `.map` and nested components rendered during that server render are exempt too. Async hooks and every non-async component are still checked.

Upstream React Compiler doesn't special-case async components yet (facebook/react#34834 is still open), so this is a small deliberate divergence. Happy to narrow it (for example, only the component body and not nested callbacks) if you'd prefer.

One note on the issue's exact snippet: on current main it isn't reported at all, because component detection ignores JSX that only appears inside a nested callback, so that function is never compiled. The false positive appears as soon as the async component has JSX the detector can see. The tests cover both shapes.

### Tests

- Pass: the issue snippet, direct `Date.now()` / `new Date()` / `Math.random()` in an async function component, async arrow and async function-expression components, impure calls in a `.map` callback and a nested helper, and a nested component.
- Fail (still reported): existing sync cases, a sync component next to an async one (only the sync one reports), a sync arrow, a `.map` callback in a sync component, `useNow`, and `async function useNow`.

`cargo test -p oxc_linter --lib rules::react::purity`, `cargo test -p oxc_react_compiler`, and `cargo lint` (warnings denied) on both crates pass locally.

issue.title: fix(linter/no-unassigned-vars): count initializers of redeclared vars as writes
issue.body:
Fixes #27982 (the `no-unassigned-vars` half; the `no-useless-concat` half is #27984).

The rule only counts `reference.is_write()` as an assignment. In Oxc a `var` initializer isn't a write reference: it's another declaration of the same symbol. So `var x; var x = k; return x;` (and the reverse order, and the `if` block case from the issue) were reported as always `undefined`, while ESLint, which records initializers as write references, reports nothing.

The rule now looks at the symbol's redeclarations and treats one as a write when its declarator has an initializer, or when it is the loop variable of a `for-in` / `for-of`. Function declarations and parameters still don't count as writes, which matches ESLint.

- Fail (still reported): `var x; var x`, a `var` after a function declaration of the same name, a `var` after a parameter of the same name, and `var { y = x }` (reads `x`, doesn't assign it).

`cargo test -p oxc_linter --lib` and `cargo lint -p oxc_linter --lib --tests` (warnings denied) pass locally.

# Why

`ExpoReactDelegate.createReactRootView` calls `createReactRootView` on every handler, even after one has already returned a root view. The sibling methods `bundleURL()` and `createRootViewController()` use `self.handlers.lazy`, so they stop at the first non-nil result. This one doesn't, because plain `compactMap` is eager.

Use `self.handlers.lazy` in `createReactRootView`, the same chain the sibling methods already use. `LazySequence.compactMap` followed by `first(where:)` only calls handlers until the first one returns a view. The fallback to `reactNativeFactory.recreateRootView` is unchanged.

- When the first handler returns a view, the second handler is never called and the factory fallback isn't used.
- When the first handler returns nil and the second returns a view, the third handler is never called.

Both would fail with the old eager `compactMap`.

issue.title: [router] Fix testing-library Jest matcher types

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: expo-router

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: PR author is not a member of the expo GitHub org

issue.body:
# Why

TypeScript rejects the `expo-router/testing-library` Jest matchers. `toHavePathname`, `toHavePathnameWithParams`, `toHaveSegments`, `toHaveSearchParams`, and `toHaveRouterState` report TS2339. The tests still pass at runtime.

The matcher types live in `src/ts-declarations/expect.d.ts`. No published entry imports that file. #36485 moved the `jest.Matchers` augmentation out of the testing-library entry. The package typecheck still includes that declaration, so the package itself compiles. A consumer that imports `expo-router/testing-library` does not see the matchers.

Fixes #51870

# How

Two solutions were possible.

1. Put `declare global` back in `src/testing-library/index.tsx`. The entry already imports `./expect` for the runtime matchers. This adds no runtime work. The matcher names then sit next to the render helpers.
2. Put `declare global` in `src/testing-library/expect.ts`. The entry already imports that module, and declaration emit keeps `import './expect'` in `build/testing-library/index.d.ts`. This adds no runtime work. issue.title: perf(deduplication): use LPOS for keepLastIfActive membership check (python)(elixir)(php)(rust)
issue.body:
keepLastIfActive copied the whole active list with LRANGE on every deduplicated add. Use LPOS instead. This shared include cannot select a script the way getState/getStateV2 do, so redis.pcall falls back to the previous scan on Redis before 6.0.6. A match at index 0 returns 0, which is truthy in Lua.

fixes #4613

  Thank you for submitting a PR!
  Please fill out all sections below to help us understand your changes.

  PR TITLE FORMAT
  ───────────────
  We use Conventional Commits: <type>(<scope>): <description>

  If your change affects one or more ports, append a tag at the end of the
  PR title (outside the conventional-commit part) to indicate their status:

    [python] / [elixir] / [php] / [rust] / [dotnet]

    (python) / (elixir) / (php) / (rust) / (dotnet)
      → The change affects that port AND Node.js.
        Multiple ports can be listed: (python)(php)

  Examples:
    fix(worker): handle stalled jobs correctly (python)(elixir)
    docs: update rate-limiting guide [python]
    feat(queue): add group priority support

  Please review all listed ports below before setting your title.
-->

### Port Impact Checklist

<!--
  Review each port and tick every box that applies.
  If a port is not affected at all, leave its box unchecked.
-->

- [x] **Python** – does this change need to be ported or documented in the Python library?
- [x] **Elixir** – does this change need to be ported or documented in the Elixir library?
- [x] **PHP** – does this change need to be ported or documented in the PHP library?
- [x] **Rust** – does this change need to be ported or documented in the Rust library?
- [ ] **.NET** – does this change need to be ported or documented in the .NET library?

The change is only in the shared Lua include `src/commands/includes/storeDeduplicatedNextJob.lua`. It is inlined through `deduplicateJob` / `deduplicateJobWithoutReplace` into `addStandardJob`, `addDelayedJob`, `addPrioritizedJob` and `addParentJob`. Every port picks it up from `rawScripts` through its `copy:lua:<port>` script, so no port source changes are needed. Python, Elixir, PHP and Rust expose `keepLastIfActive`, so their deduplicated adds take the new path. .NET ships the same scripts but appears not to pass `keepLastIfActive` (its storage opts don't include `deduplication`), so it isn't ticked.

### Why

<!--
  1. Why is this change necessary?
  2. What problem does it solve or improve?
  3. Link to any relevant issues, if applicable.
-->

With `deduplication: { keepLastIfActive: true }`, every deduplicated add while the original job may be active called `LRANGE active 0 -1`. That copied the whole active list into the Lua VM just to check whether one id was in it. On queues with many active jobs, this made each deduplicated add O(N) in both memory and copying (#4613).

### How

<!--
  1. How did you implement this?
  2. Outline the approach or steps taken.
  3. List any resources or documentation that helped you.
-->

- Use `LPOS activeKey currentDeduplicatedJobId`, which scans the list in C and returns the index or nil, without copying the list.
- `getState`/`getStateV2` pick an LPOS-based script at the TypeScript call site based on the Redis version (>= 6.0.6). This include is shared by several scripts and can't be swapped that way. So it probes with `redis.pcall('LPOS', …)`. If Redis returns an error table (older Redis without LPOS), it falls back to the previous `LRANGE` + `checkItemInList` scan.
- A hit at index 0 returns `0`, which is truthy in Lua. Only `nil`/`false` count as a miss, so a plain `if pos then` check is correct without a `> 0` comparison.

### Additional Notes (Optional)

<!--
  Use this space for additional considerations:
  - Potential side effects
  - Dependencies
  - Testing instructions
  - Anything else reviewers should know
-->

New tests in `tests/deduplication.test.ts`. A `placeOnActiveList` helper, defined as a Lua command so every Redis adapter runs the same setup, places a job on the active list at a chosen position:
- `stores the next job when the deduplicated job is at index 0 of the active list`: asserts `LPOS` returns `0` and the next job is still stored in `dn:<id>`.
- `stores the next job when the deduplicated job is active past index 0` (index 2).
- `does not store a next job when other jobs are active but this one is not`: `LPOS` returns null, no `dn:<id>` entry, and the proposed job isn't created.
- The existing `should still deduplicate when dedup job is waiting (not active)` test now also asserts that no next-job entry is stored.

No behavior change is intended: the same membership result, only cheaper on Redis >= 6.0.6.

issue.title: fix(migrations): serialize concurrent migrator runs
issue.body:
Concurrent `migrator.up()` / `migrator.down()` calls could both apply the same data migration. Each run now takes a lock for the whole call, then reads the executed set, so the waiter applies nothing that the first run already logged.

- PostgreSQL (and PGlite): session `pg_advisory_lock`, held on a pinned connection. `lock_timeout` and `statement_timeout` are cleared only while waiting, then restored.
- MySQL and MariaDB: `GET_LOCK` with a large positive timeout. MariaDB treats a negative timeout as invalid and would not lock.
- SQL Server: session `sp_getapplock`.
- File-backed SQLite: a lock file beside the database. `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on a second connection would block the migration's own writes.

The lock name is the migrations table (schema + table). In-memory SQLite is not shared across connections. Oracle has no unprivileged session lock, so two Oracle processes can still race.

Closes #8456

issue.title: fix(postgres): reject a commit PostgreSQL answered with ROLLBACK
issue.body:
PostgreSQL does not raise when `COMMIT` runs in an aborted transaction. The command tag is `ROLLBACK` and every write is discarded. `pg` resolves that query, Kysely drops the tag, and `AbstractSqlConnection.commit()` treated resolution as success, so `em.transactional()` / `em.commit()` resolved and `afterTransactionCommit` fired.

The postgres driver now rejects that `COMMIT` while the tag is still visible and rolls the Kysely transaction back so the pooled client is released. The failure is a `DriverException`. A nested savepoint rollback is unchanged: its outer `COMMIT` still has the tag `COMMIT`.

Tests: `tests/issues/GH8476.test.ts` (9 tests) covers `em.transactional()`, `em.commit()`, a joined `REQUIRED` transaction, a nested savepoint that must still commit, and a raw `COMMIT` whose command tag is `ROLLBACK`. The PostgreSQL entity-manager and transaction-propagation suites, `GH1175`, the PostgreSQL connection tests and the SQLite transaction suites also pass, along with `yarn lint` and `yarn build`.

Closes #8476

issue.title: fix(core): do not crash when raw mode cannot be enabled
issue.body:
Entering raw mode fails with ENXIO when stdout is a tty, stdin is not, and the process has no controlling terminal. Treat that failure as non-fatal and skip restoring raw mode so the task still runs.

<!-- Please make sure you have read the submission guidelines before posting an PR -->
<!-- https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#-submitting-a-pr -->

## Current Behavior
<!-- This is the behavior we have today -->

When stdout is a tty but stdin is not (for example `</dev/null`) and the process has no controlling terminal (a new session via `setsid`, or the Nix build sandbox), `PseudoTerminal::run_command` calls `enable_raw_mode().expect(...)`. crossterm falls back to opening `/dev/tty`, which fails with ENXIO, so nx panics with `Failed to enter raw terminal mode: ... No such device or address` and aborts before the task runs.

Repro: `setsid --wait npx nx run hello:hello </dev/null`

## Expected Behavior
<!-- This is the behavior we should expect with the changes in this PR -->

Raw mode is optional in that environment. If `enable_raw_mode` fails, nx logs it at trace level, does not try to restore raw mode afterwards, and runs the task normally.

issue.title: fix(solid): render a resolved lazy() component synchronously on remount
issue.body:
Disposing a lazy() instance cleared the shared component cache even after the module had loaded, so the next mount rendered nothing or the Suspense fallback. Only release that cache while it still points at the in-flight resource.

Fixes #4118

<!--
  Thanks for submitting a pull request!
  We appreciate you spending the time to work on these changes. Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. The three fields below are mandatory.

  Before submitting a pull request, please make sure the following is done:

  1. Fork [the repository](https://github.com/solidjs/solid) and create your branch from `main`.
  2. Run `pnpm i` in the repository root.
  3. If you've fixed a bug or added code that should be tested, add tests!
  4. You should run `pnpm build` before running any tests as it copies some files in that are required for Solid to work.
  5. Ensure the test suite passes (`pnpm test`).
  6. Format your code with [prettier](https://github.com/prettier/prettier).
  7. Commit with conventional commits standards
-->

## Summary

<!--
 Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve?
-->

Since 1.9.14, disposing any instance of a `lazy()` component clears the module-level `comp` cache that all instances share (#4118). Clearing it is right while the import is still in flight or has failed, because then the load can be collected and retried. But it also ran after the import had resolved. So the next mount of an already-loaded component made a new resource and rendered `""` until it resolved, or showed the `<Suspense>` fallback again. In 1.9.13 that remount rendered synchronously. Users see it as a flash when a lazily loaded page or overlay is closed and reopened.

The fix is in `packages/solid/src/render/component.ts`. Once `load()` resolves, it replaces `comp` with the loaded component. The `onCleanup` now clears `comp` only if it still points at this instance's resource:

```ts
onCleanup(() => {
  if (comp === s) comp = undefined;
});
```

So:
- An in-flight or rejected import is still released when its owner is disposed, and the next mount retries it. This keeps the behavior from 1.9.14.
- A resolved module stays cached, and the next mount renders synchronously, both with and without `<Suspense>`. This brings back the 1.9.13 behavior.

A changeset (`solid-js`: patch) is included.

## How did you test this change?

<!--
  Demonstrate the code is solid. Example: The exact commands you ran and their output, screenshots / videos if the pull request changes the user interface.
  How exactly did you verify that your PR solves the issue you wanted to solve?
-->

Two tests were added to `packages/solid/web/test/lazy.spec.tsx` (`lazy() disposal` suite):

- **`remounting an already-loaded lazy() component renders synchronously`**: the #4118 repro as a test. A `lazy()` component is mounted in a `createRoot`, its import is flushed, the root is disposed, and the component is mounted again. The test expects `"loaded"` right away on the second mount, with no flush. It covers both a bare `lazy()` and one inside `<Suspense fallback="fallback">`.
- **`a rejected lazy() import is retried after its root is disposed`**: the first import rejects under an `ErrorBoundary` (`error:network error`, 1 attempt). The root is disposed, and the next mount loads successfully (`loaded`, 2 attempts). This guards the retry behavior that the original cleanup was added for.

The existing `lazy() retries import function on subsequent load if previous promise rejected` test is unchanged.

```sh
pnpm i
pnpm build
pnpm test
```

issue.title: [android][audio] Pass AudioSource headers through AudioPlaylist

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: PR author is not a member of the expo GitHub org

issue.body:
# Why

Fixes #51434.

On Android, `AudioPlaylist` does not send `AudioSource.headers` with remote track requests. The same source plays from `AudioPlayer` and fails from a playlist when the server requires those headers.

`AudioPlaylist` adds each track as a bare `MediaItem` and loads every track through one `DefaultDataSource` factory. That factory has no per-source headers. `AudioPlayer` builds a `MediaSource` per source and passes `source.headers` into `httpDataSourceFactory`.

# How

Each playlist track now uses `AudioModule.createMediaItem`, the same path `AudioPlayer` uses. For `http` and `https`, that path builds an `OkHttpDataSource` factory and calls `setDefaultRequestProperties` with `AudioSource.headers`. The playlist adds the resulting `MediaSource` with `addMediaSource` for the initial queue, `add`, and `insert`.

One player-wide factory cannot carry different headers for each track. Per-track media sources keep the player behavior for local files, raw resources, HLS, DASH, and SmoothStreaming.

# Test Plan

- Confirmed on `main` that `AudioPlaylist` still receives `DefaultDataSource.Factory(context)` and adds bare `MediaItem`s, while `createMediaItem` passes `source.headers` into `httpDataSourceFactory`.

issue.body:
Spread every valid SVG prop from a data entry onto its sector, except id, and merge those props over the chart props. A fill or stroke on the chart or the entry turns the theme colors off; a fill inherited from a parent does not.

## Description

<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->

Replaces `getSectorStyles` in `src/chart/SunburstChart.tsx` with a standalone `resolveSectorProps`:

- **All valid SVG props from the data entry are spread on the sector, in both modes.** This includes `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `strokeDasharray`, `opacity`, `className`, `style` and `data-*`. They are filtered with `svgPropertiesNoEventsFromUnknown`. `id` is always removed so a data id can't end up on a sector. Non-SVG keys are dropped.
- **Entry props merge over chart props.** A value the entry leaves out comes from `<SunburstChart>`. Previously, without a theme, only `fill` came from data and `stroke` always came from props or defaults.
- **Chart colors turn the theme off.** A `fill` or `stroke` on `<SunburstChart>` now disables the theme colors, the same as for Line, Area, Bar, Scatter, Radar, RadialBar, Pie and Funnel. - **An inherited fill doesn't count as the child's own color.** A child with no color of its own still paints with its parent's fill. It still counts as uncolored, so it keeps the theme separator (`pageBackground`) stroke.

issue.body:
# Why

On web, `<Link href="/second" asChild>` throws in development and renders a blank screen in production when the child passes a style array, such as `<Pressable style={[styles.button, styles.highlighted]}>`.

`ShimSlotForReactNative` flattens the Link style, then passes the child to Radix `Slot`. Radix merges `style` with `{ ...slotStyle, ...childStyle }`. That spread turns an array into `{0: …, 1: …}`. react-dom then throws `Failed to set an indexed property [0] on 'CSSStyleDeclaration'`.

#41901 only added the development throw. The check is removed in production, so the screen stays blank. This does not handle style functions. #50673 covers that case.

Fixes #51763

# How

Flatten the child style with `StyleSheet.flatten` before Radix merges props. Radix then spreads an object, and the child values still override the Link style on the same keys.

The flatten runs in development and in production. It runs only when the child style is an array, so a style function is left as it is today. #50673 can still hoist a function in this shim. The Slot's own `StyleSheet.flatten(style)` call is unchanged.

The diff updates `packages/expo-router/src/ui/Slot.tsx`, the iOS and web Link tests, and adds a patch changeset.

# Test Plan

Wrote the assertions first. On upstream `main` they failed with `[expo-router]: You are passing an array of styles to a child of <Slot>...`.

- iOS, Web, and Node, those cases: 6 failed, 94 skipped.
- After the fix, those 6 passed. A child array with no Link style renders both values. A child array merged with a Link style keeps the Link-only keys, and the child wins on shared keys (`backgroundColor: 'red'` over `'blue'`).
- `pnpm exec jest src/link src/ui`: 23 suites passed, 268 passed, 1 skipped, 25 snapshots passed.
- `pnpm exec jest` for the whole package: 460 suites passed, 5995 passed, 9 skipped, 257 snapshots passed, 8 projects.
- `pnpm run typecheck` passed. `pnpm run lint` passed.

No simulator, emulator, or browser run. The web Jest project uses react-native-web and react-dom, which is the path that threw `CSSStyleDeclaration`.

No browser screenshots. The web Jest project renders the child with both styles.
